reason: Batch of independently reviewed PRs, each green on its own: #1030: After a worker-start timeout, auto-admission kept the prepared worker's runtime ID until an attach fully succeeded and blocked the project until the host or memory-policy revision changed, with no time-based retry. An attach that timed out after the grant committed left the ID behind; once that worker retired, the next readmission re-attached the dead process (connection refused) and the project stayed without a worker until Core restarted. A prepared worker is now forgotten only on SQL evidence (owns the project, not attachable, or serves another project), failed admissions retry with a bounded backoff (and at once on a revision change) without starving other projects, diagnostics name the project and attempt and flag a persistent failure, and the attach wait tolerates a slow status read within its bound. Rebased onto #1028 (queued project commands admit a worker) and #1032 (no claim onto a worker an aborted shutdown closed): the demand query keeps #1028's queued-work demand, archived-with-work admission and retirement-hold exclusion, and adds this change's backoff exclusion. Selection covers the stale-worker readmission, backoff without a revision change, the persistent-failure diagnostic, the slow status read, #1028's chatless edit/archived delete admission, retirement and ingress-wait cases and its retirement contract tests, #1032's aborted-shutdown claim and retirement cases, and the existing admission, readmission, held-project, auto-recovery and API worker cases. #1037: Ask Nebula could not open over any conversation or with a harness assistant: #939 made ChatService.session_messages and HarnessRuntimeService.create_session async but POST /chat/temporary-sessions still called both without await (TypeError 'coroutine' object is not subscriptable / AttributeError on harness.model/.id). The fix awaits both. Selected: the popup route suite (its create() helper now awaits the client, the harness fork test awaits an AsyncMock, and two new tests drive the real route over a real HarnessRuntimeService), the execution-scope suite with the new worker-context Ask Nebula route test (provider and harness, the route a project worker runs for this chat-start command), and the expired-popup collector case of the same router. #1039: #939 made ControlAssistantWork.chat_detail and require_plan and ChatQueueService.get async, but ButlerAuthorityService.dispatch/_reconcile still called them without await, so every planned Butler Steer/Delegate/Act action raised AttributeError before dispatch, stayed planned, and the oversight loop recorded butler.project_replay_failed every 30 s (skipping recovery and memory capture). The fix awaits the four calls and types the work dependency so mypy sees them. Selected: test_butler_authority.py (repaired test-side awaits plus three new regressions, including the running oversight worker behind an authenticated Steer grant; 13 of its 16 tests fail on main because of this defect), test_butler_tool_failures.py (the third action trigger; its parent steer fails on main with the same AttributeError once the test awaits its own calls), and the unchanged suites around the oversight loop that pass on pristine origin/main under CI's warning flags: test_butler_recovery.py, test_butler_memory_pivotal.py, test_butler_capacity_retry.py, test_butler_project_roster.py, test_async_caller_boundaries.py and the 17 passing test_butler_oversight.py cases. #1026: A harness goal turn's cleanup posts pending subagent reports before settling the goal; a posted report can start the goal's next turn, advancing its step and moving its execution claim. The older turn's _settle_goal_turn then paused the goal for the newer turn's step budget mid-turn and cleared that turn's claim, so a completion it proposed was refused. _settle_goal_turn now leaves a goal claimed by another turn to that turn and _pause_goal re-checks ownership per attempt. The flaky test_late_subagent_report_resumes_parked_harness_goal_once (failing ~half of runs on main) waited on _chat_turn_tasks emptying, which precedes settle; it now awaits the turn task. A new deterministic test covers a report arriving before the earlier turn settles. Selected: harness and provider goal suites and single-active harness chat. #1024: ChatQueueService.run woke every 0.5 s in every execution worker and each pass opened a worker transaction under the global execution advisory lock, about 70 % of an idle worker's lock acquisitions. The dispatcher now waits for a NebulaStore.on_follow_up_change signal (queue writes; turn activity in conversations whose queue waits on a turn), keeps the 0.5 s recheck only while a queue waits on a running response, parks queues that only wait for a turn status change (linked reviews, and follow-ups behind their own or the conversation's latest response awaiting an approval or callback), runs a 30 s safety pass and retries failed queue reads. Selected: the follow-up dispatcher and polling-cost tests (new run()-driven wake, end-to-end dispatch, parking, unrelated-activity, safety-pass, read-failure and store-signal tests), every follow-up queue test and the store transaction suites, because NebulaStore.transaction now signals from a finally block. #1041: An API sends a streaming chat as chat.accept/v1 only when the project's current owner declares it; a cold project (no owner after a Core start or idle retirement) gets http.invoke/v1, whose streamed response the owner serves for the whole turn while the project's ordered work lane waits (renames/archives/other sends waited up to 17 minutes under host pressure). The kernel now publishes its typed chat transports and the owner's DurableHttpRunner renames a claimed http.invoke chat start to chat.accept/v1 or chat.resume/v1 under its fence (new RuntimeCoordination.retype_chat_start) before invoking it. Review fixes: chat_binding reads the binding before the command (no final-looking 409 across a rename), and a failed rename keeps the HTTP transport instead of going uncertain. Selected: chat acceptance (new tests incl. Postgres variants), delivery, coordination, execution worker, acceptance compatibility and API worker suites. #1038: Brings the GUI's chat lifecycle actions to the paired terminal client: collapsed thinking with /thinking and on-demand saved reasoning; per-turn elapsed time and token usage on answer headings; edit-and-resend that rewinds only when the edit is sent; /search over saved messages (conversation or project, bookmarked only) opening the match; /bookmark; /side side chats without tools; /chat bulk with Core verification; /chat finish for a provider answer that stopped early and a linked harness retry; pinned/flag/archived markers and whole-catalog search in /chats. Selected: the new conversations unit contracts, the shell and TUI presentation suites, the client wheel allowlist (new module), two new real paired TLS LAN Core PTY journeys, the product-knowledge search and Chroma digest sync, the settings-catalog terminal discovery test, and existing real-Core cases covering send/stream, the slash menu order, settings, remembered chats and the project picker.
